## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There is no evidence yet. The starting network scored 0/0, so it is not yet clear whether the network, the recipe or both are at fault. The starting network can in principle represent "brick lands at layer L and fills only target cells": a 1x1 stem over the per-layer channels, then max/min/avg pooling over each footprint. The default recipe gives only 32 PPO updates of 4096 samples, which is very few policy-improvement steps, so the recipe is a likely bottleneck. Round 1 therefore tests two recipe directions on the unchanged network: more, smaller updates (A), and fewer epochs with more fresh samples (C). It also tests one network change under recipe A's settings (B): a network that works layer by layer, scores each brick at every layer and learns a soft weighting over the layer it lands on. A versus B separates the network effect; A versus C separates the recipe effect.

### Round 2
All three round-1 trials scored exactly 0 on dev and 0 on training success: the baseline with smaller updates, a per-layer net with a landing gate, and the baseline with 2 PPO epochs (231k steps). Neither more updates nor almost twice as many samples moved anything off zero, so the bottleneck is probably not the sample count alone. The task says this world may not behave as described. All three nets build placement logits from footprint pooling that assumes a top-left anchor and the stated brick shapes, so a mismatch in action layout would make placement impossible to learn. The per-cell route to the policy and value is also weak at seeing the whole design. This round tests three ways of removing that assumption: a learned 3x3 placement head with the mask as an input; a fully connected head that assumes no layout at all; and global attention over cells. All three use the cheap 2-epoch recipe so the results compare cleanly.

### Round 3
All six trials scored exactly 0, on dev and on training success. That covers recipe tweaks to the baseline, a per-layer landing gate, a learned 3x3 head, a flatten-MLP head and a cell transformer. Because there is no gradient of results, the architecture comparisons so far tell us nothing. Two explanations fit. (1) The budget is too small: about 125k–240k steps is roughly 10–20k episodes, which may never produce a full exact build and so never teaches the agent DONE. (2) The world differs from the description, for example in action layout or anchor, so heads that assume a spatial layout learn nothing. I can't tell these apart yet. This round pushes sample count to the limit (1 PPO epoch gives about 320–426k steps) and keeps 2048-sample updates with 64-sample minibatches, so there are many updates and gradient steps. The three candidates cover a spatially aligned head (baseline), a layout-agnostic head (flatten MLP) and a hybrid with a zero-initialised flat residual. Whichever gets off zero shows whether data or layout is the bottleneck.

### Round 4
All 9 trials scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success. They covered pooled, 3x3, transformer and flatten heads, 1 to 4 PPO epochs and up to 426k steps. Training success never left zero for any network, including the head that makes no assumption about how actions map to cells. So the shared bottleneck is probably the recipe or exploration, not the network.

Every trial kept lr 1e-3. All but the starting run used entropy 0.003, and nothing tried entropy above 0.01. A likely failure mode is early collapse onto DONE or onto a few safe placements: random placements tend to fill cells outside the target, which costs reward, while DONE costs nothing. If the policy collapses there, it never reaches an exact build and never sees the +1 bonus. Gamma 0.95 also discounts that terminal bonus.

This last round tests the untried settings: higher entropy, a longer horizon, a lower learning rate and a higher one, and a wider receptive field.
